findings.title: Missing authentication check on getDownloadFileSignedURL operation
findings.description: The getDownloadFileSignedURL operation in file-upload/operations.ts does not validate that the requesting user owns the file before generating a download URL. This allows any authenticated user to generate download URLs for any file in the system by guessing or knowing S3 keys.
findings.suggested_fix: Add authentication and authorization check: (1) Verify context.user exists with `if (!context.user) throw new HttpError(401)`. (2) Query the File entity to verify the file belongs to the authenticated user before generating the URL: `const file = await context.entities.File.findUnique({ where: { s3Key }, select: { userId: true } }); if (!file || file.userId !== context.user.id) throw new HttpError(403, 'File not found or access denied');`

findings.title: Missing RBAC check for admin dashboard access
findings.description: Admin dashboard pages (UsersDashboardPage, AnalyticsDashboardPage, SettingsPage) accept a user parameter but do not validate that the user has admin privileges. Any authenticated user who can navigate to /admin URLs could potentially access sensitive admin data.
findings.suggested_fix: Add admin role validation at the beginning of each admin page component: `if (!user.isAdmin) return <Navigate to="/" />`. Additionally, ensure the Wasp main.wasp file has `authRequired: true` set on all admin page routes. For server-side queries like getDailyStats, verify `if (!context.user?.isAdmin) throw new HttpError(403, 'Admin access required')` in the operation handler.

findings.title: Unauthenticated access to getDailyStats analytics query
findings.description: The getDailyStats operation is called from AnalyticsDashboardPage without visible authentication enforcement in the client code. If the server-side operation lacks proper authentication checks, sensitive analytics data could be exposed.

locations.snippet: const { data: stats, isLoading, error } = useQuery(getDailyStats);

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure getDailyStats operation (defined in server operations, not shown in provided code) has: (1) Authentication check: `if (!context.user) throw new HttpError(401)`. (2) Admin authorization check: `if (!context.user.isAdmin) throw new HttpError(403, 'Admin access required')`. (3) Mark the route as `authRequired: true` in main.wasp configuration.

findings.title: Cross-user file access via direct S3 key manipulation
findings.description: The FileUploadPage allows users to download files by setting s3Key state, which is then used in getDownloadFileSignedURL. Since getDownloadFileSignedURL doesn't validate file ownership, a user could modify the S3 key in browser DevTools to download other users' files.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the file ID (not S3 key) to the download function instead: (1) Change download logic to pass file `id` instead of `s3Key`: `refetchDownloadUrl({ fileId: file.id })`. (2) Update getDownloadFileSignedURL to accept fileId, query the File entity, verify ownership, then generate the signed URL. This prevents users from bypassing ownership checks via direct S3 key manipulation.

findings.title: Weak password reset token validation flow
findings.description: The PasswordResetPage and RequestPasswordResetPage components use Wasp's built-in auth forms (ResetPasswordForm, ForgotPasswordForm) without visible token validation logic in the provided code. If the backend doesn't properly validate reset token expiration and one-time use, attackers could reuse or forge tokens.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify in Wasp's server-side auth configuration that: (1) Password reset tokens have a short expiration time (typically 15-30 minutes). (2) Tokens are single-use and deleted/invalidated immediately after being used. (3) Token generation uses cryptographically secure random values. (4) Tokens are stored securely (hashed) in the database. These are typically Wasp framework features, but confirm in main.wasp that `email.passwordResetTokenExpirationInMinutes` is set appropriately and token reuse is prevented.

findings.title: Admin role assignment based on email without validation
findings.description: The userSignupFields.ts file sets isAdmin=true based on matching email addresses from an ADMIN_EMAILS environment variable. However, there's no verification that the email is actually verified before assigning admin privileges, and email verification could be bypassed.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement post-signup email verification before granting admin access: (1) Initially set isAdmin=false for all signups. (2) After email verification is confirmed via EmailVerificationPage, have an admin manually verify and promote the user. (3) Alternatively, use a separate admin provisioning flow that requires verification. (4) For email-based auth methods, ensure the isAdmin assignment only happens after `emailVerified: true` is confirmed in the Wasp auth context.

findings.title: Email verification token sent in plaintext via email
findings.description: The getVerificationEmailContent function in emails.ts sends the full verification link (which includes the token) in plaintext in the email body. If email is intercepted or logs are accessed, the token is exposed.
findings.suggested_fix: This is inherent to email verification flows and Wasp handles this securely by default. However, ensure: (1) Verification links use HTTPS-only URLs. (2) Verification tokens are generated with `crypto.randomBytes()` or similar. (3) Tokens have short expiration (5-24 hours). (4) Consider adding rate limiting on email verification endpoints to prevent brute force. (5) Log email sends but never log the actual token/link. Wasp framework typically implements these, but verify in main.wasp configuration.

findings.title: OAuth provider email verification bypass for GitHub
findings.description: In getGitHubUserFields, the isAdmin check verifies email is verified, but the primary login flow doesn't enforce verified email status. A user could potentially register via GitHub without a verified email and later gain access to email-gated features.
findings.suggested_fix: Ensure email verification status is checked for all OAuth providers, not just for admin assignment: (1) Add a check in signup flow: `if (!emailInfo.verified) throw new Error('Email must be verified with GitHub')`. (2) Require unverified email users to verify via the app's email verification flow before accessing paid/restricted features. (3) Store emailVerified status in the User entity and enforce it at operation level, not just component level.

findings.title: Missing authentication on payment webhook endpoints
findings.description: The webhook.ts file exports paymentsWebhook and paymentsMiddlewareConfigFn, which should rely on signature verification from payment providers. However, if signature validation is misconfigured or missing, attackers could forge webhook events to grant subscriptions or credits without payment.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify in the specific payment processor webhook implementations (Stripe, LemonSqueezy, Polar) that: (1) All webhook events are validated using the provider's signature verification (e.g., Stripe uses `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()`). (2) Webhook secrets are stored in environment variables and never hardcoded. (3) Webhook endpoint is registered with the payment processor to prevent forgery. (4) Only trusted event types are processed. Stripe webhook example at stripe/webhook.ts should have `stripe.webhooks.constructEvent()` call; verify it's present and properly configured.

findings.title: User data leakage in error messages on failed auth
findings.description: Auth pages (LoginPage, SignupPage) use Wasp's built-in auth forms which may expose whether an email exists in the system through different error messages (e.g., 'User already exists' vs 'Invalid credentials').
findings.suggested_fix: Review Wasp's authentication error handling. If possible in main.wasp configuration: (1) Use generic error messages on login failure ('Invalid email or password') instead of distinguishing between 'user not found' and 'wrong password'. (2) Ensure signup returns generic success message whether email exists or not. (3) For password reset, return generic 'Check your email' regardless of whether the email exists. (4) Implement rate limiting to prevent email enumeration attacks on login/signup endpoints.

findings.title: Insufficient input validation on S3 key generation
findings.description: The getS3Key function in s3Utils.ts uses user-supplied fileName to construct the S3 key. While it extracts only the extension, a malicious filename could still cause issues (e.g., path traversal attempts, although S3 keys are flat).
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the file extension more strictly: (1) Only allow extensions from the ALLOWED_FILE_TYPES list, not just any extension. (2) Sanitize extension to prevent injection: `const ext = path.extname(fileName).slice(1).toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '');`. (3) Add maximum length check to prevent DoS: `if (fileName.length > 255) throw new Error('Filename too long');`. (4) The current approach is already relatively safe since path traversal is mitigated by using randomUUID, but explicit validation is better practice.

findings.title: Missing rate limiting on payment operations
findings.description: The generateCheckoutSession operation can be called repeatedly without rate limiting, potentially allowing attackers to create numerous checkout sessions (DoS) or spam payment provider APIs.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement rate limiting on payment operations: (1) Add a rate limiter middleware in Wasp configuration (if available) to limit generateCheckoutSession to N requests per user per time window (e.g., 5 requests per 5 minutes). (2) Alternatively, track recent checkout sessions in cache/database and reject if user has created too many in a time window. (3) Log checkout session creation attempts for fraud detection. (4) Consider adding CAPTCHA for repeated failed checkout attempts.

pass_results.pass_summary: Found 2 critical severity issues (unauthenticated file download URL generation, missing admin RBAC), 4 high severity issues (unauthenticated analytics query, cross-user file access, weak password reset validation, OAuth email verification bypass), 4 medium severity issues (email verification token exposure, payment webhook auth, auth error message info leakage, payment operation rate limiting), and 1 low severity issue (S3 key validation). Critical findings require immediate remediation to prevent unauthorized data access and privilege escalation.

Found 1 critical, 5 high, 4 medium, and 2 low severity data handling issues. Critical issue: unvalidated S3 key download allowing unauthorized file access. High issues: missing admin role checks in dashboard access. Medium issues include file upload validation, payment webhook CSRF, file name validation, and rate limiting gaps. Most findings are actionable with specific code examples.

Found 6 critical and 10 high severity infrastructure security issues. Most critical: missing HTTPS enforcement, no rate limiting on auth/file upload, lack of CSP headers, dependency vulnerability scanning, and incomplete webhook validation. High severity issues include missing CORS configuration, admin role enforcement at backend, and unvalidated file uploads. Medium severity issues involve verbose error messages, missing security headers, and analytics data exposure.
